record_type_quote: We examined whether findings of Kavussanu et al. (2022), who developed and evaluated a psychological intervention in British and Greek athletes would be replicated in a sample of Italian athletes; we also extended previous research by adding a no-treatment control group.

targets.authors: Kavussanu, M., Barkoukis, V., Hurst, P., Yukhymenko-Lescroart, M., Skoufa, L., Chirico, A., Lucidi, F., & Ring, C.
targets.title: A psychological intervention reduces doping likelihood in British and Greek athletes: Evidence from a randomised controlled trial.
targets.evidence_quote: We examined whether findings of Kavussanu et al. (2022), who developed and evaluated a psychological intervention in British and Greek athletes would be replicated in a sample of Italian athletes; we also extended previous research by adding a no-treatment control group.
targets.outcome_quote: In conclusion, our study broadly replicates previous findings and highlights the need for anti-doping organizations to target psychological variables and doping-relevant information in anti-doping education.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly conclude that the study broadly replicates previous findings as a whole. This overall verdict controls despite some secondary results differing. The primary doping-likelihood finding is replicated.

reasoning: Independent Italian athlete sample explicitly retests Kavussanu et al. (2022), adding a no-treatment control. The 2021 moral-intervention paper is discussed as earlier context and supporting comparison, but this study implements and explicitly targets the 2022 psychological intervention. Other intervention evaluations cited as background are not additional targets.
